The new nvim-ts main branch removes a lot of the functionality and brings many performance improvements, but it is not the default branch for now, and won't be for a while. Though, after 0.10 master is pretty much deprecated, and plugins should not depend on nvim-ts utilities besides locals...this will also allow users to use the main branch without these plugins breaking. Thanks!

comment_regular_data.body:
Note: `locals.lua` is also not guaranteed to be kept in nvim-treesitter 1.0; only the queries will (most likely) be maintained. To be clear: going forward, **no plugin should be explicitly depending on nvim-treesitter**.

If there are (widely) useful utility functions missing, they should be considered for inclusion in the core API.

> The new nvim-ts main branch removes a lot of the functionality and brings many performance improvements, but it is not the default branch for now, and won't be for a while. Though, after 0.10 master is pretty much deprecated, and plugins should not depend on nvim-ts utilities besides locals...this will also allow users to use the main branch without these plugins breaking. Thanks!

Thanks the PR!

To be honest, I am not keen on making braking changes for the not stable work-in-progress branch which is not the default yet. Besides, all proposed changes address tree-sitter based functionality which can choose what approach to use through `opts.use_nvim_treesitter`. If users want/need to use `main` 'nvim-treesitter' branch, I'd recommend using `opts.use_nvim_treesitter = false` for now.

@clason, the one utility function used in 'mini.ai' and 'mini.surround' which I can not find in Nightly is `require('nvim-treesitter.query').get_capture_matches_recursively()`. Is this considered to be a (widely) used utility function?

Is this a breaking change though? The user-facing behavior should not change, except that users can (but don't have to) drop nvim-treesitter if they "bring their own parser".

> require('nvim-treesitter.query').get_capture_matches_recursively(). Is this considered to be a (widely) used utility function?

Not sure; if someone were to make a PR, a quick GH search would tell them. It would also depend on whether this can be easily replicated using already provided functions.

> Is this a breaking change though? The user-facing behavior should not change, except that users can (but don't have to) drop nvim-treesitter if they "bring their own parser".

I would assume that such change would require new tree-sitter utilities ported from 'nvim-treesitter' into Neovim core, which makes it a hard dependence on nightly (hence breaking for others Neovim versions). The code in PR seems like a direct copy-paste from 'nvim-treesitter' source code, so can't judge beyond that.
It is just copy-pasted (slightly adjusted), so it wouldn't be breaking for now

> It is just copy-pasted (slightly adjusted), so it wouldn't be breaking for now

As is, it won't work because it uses too much of 'nvim-treesitter' code: some `M` module, `M.iter_group_results`, `utils.get_at_path`.
I'll later do more research to see the best course of action here.
That being said, there's no particular urgency; the deprecation of the legacy nvim-treesitter won't be happening until after the Nvim 0.10 release, probably sometime (late) this summer.

> It is just copy-pasted (slightly adjusted), so it wouldn't be breaking for now

Yeah, that's not good enough; you need an actual refactor of the calling code based on current Neovim API. I'd recommend closing this PR and trying again later.
the adjusted bit is adjusted for the current Neovim API (so I guess it is breaking, requiring neovim from whenever vim.treesitter.get_parser was added)
You did not adjust the actual code at all (or sufficiently, it looks like); just a copy-paste leaving references to -- uncopied -- internal nvim-treesitter code...
oh yeah...I relied on lsp too much, will close for now, my bad

@amaanq If you permit me to be blunt: this PR is a bit of an ill-considered hip shot. The first step should be to look at our own `nvim-treesitter-textobjects` and do a proper refactor of this (in a separate `main` branch). After this is done (possibly including upstreaming utility functions), we can take the lessons learned to the broader ecosystem.
yeah that's a good idea, that'd also give me a better sense of how to refactor for nvim-ts main going forward
